capabilities: Convert attachments (PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, email, images) to Markdown with YAML frontmatter
Transcribe audio and video recordings on-device into structured meeting summaries
Convert clipboard content into a new note via the command palette
Track note maturity with Grades (Blank to Gem) shown in an info bar and status bar
Surface hub notes as Condensers and show Bond counts from the link graph
extras: Desktop-only and macOS-only; the companion Thunderegg app is closed source (the plugin itself is MIT). Freemium: conversion is free and unlimited, Pro is a $19.95 one-time purchase, no account. README includes detailed privacy disclosures: no network calls by default, on-device conversion and transcription, optional Canvas publish is the only plugin network feature.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to turn PDFs, Office files, images, emails or meeting recordings into clean Markdown notes with frontmatter.

relations.evidence: This plugin is the Obsidian half; the Thunderegg app does the converting
Image OCR uses the Apple Vision ocr helper that ships with the Thunderegg app

requires.name: Thunderegg Pro ($19.95 once) for meeting recording, transcription and AI write-up

summary: Attachment-to-Markdown converter that shells out to a local macOS engine, plus a Refinery layer that tracks note maturity and link-based connections.
